Date: 2026-11-15
Status: Accepted

## Context

Agents need to own active tickets and receive assignment notifications. Existing data files and weekly reports must continue working.

## Decision

We store a nullable assignee on every ticket and expose assignment through PUT /tickets/:id/assignee.
Only open and in-progress tickets can change assignment. The store audits real changes and enqueues a notification
for each new assignment, using the audit sequence in its key so pending assignments never suppress later changes.
Old data records without an assignee load as null. Raw CLI output appends assignee after its existing four columns.
All listing filters must match together.

## Consequences

Assignments survive restarts, notifications use the worker's existing retries, and report column positions stay stable.
An unchanged assignment produces no audit entry or notification. Older service versions do not preserve the new field.
''')

Send `{ "tickets": [...] }`, with zero to 5000 items using the same fields and validation as `POST /tickets`.

Path('docs/decisions/0009-atomic-ticket-import.md').write_text('''# 9. Atomic ticket import

Status: Accepted

## Context

Moving from the old tracker requires up to 5000 tickets per request, preserving order and the usual creation effects.
Saving the entire data file for every ticket would repeatedly serialize a growing state and delay large imports.

## Decision

Validate every input first and report the first invalid array index. The store stages all creation effects using
its shared creation routine, saves the completed state once, then adopts it. The existing JSON data format and
notification worker remain in use. Empty imports perform no write. The import route has a minimum 16 MiB body
allowance to hold 5000 maximum-length inputs even with escaped Unicode.

## Consequences

Validation errors consume no ids or side effects. Persistence errors leave the original in-memory state intact.
Imports require transient memory for a staged copy of the current state. Single-ticket requests retain their
existing limits and behavior.
''')
p=Path('docs/decisions/README.md');p.write_text(p.read_text()+'| 9 | [Atomic ticket import](0009-atomic-ticket-import.md) | Accepted |\n')

p=Path('docs/operations.md');s=p.read_text();s+='''
## Due-time rollout

1. Stop the existing service and back up `DATA_FILE`. Choose the response hours through `RESPONSE_HOURS_URGENT`,
   `RESPONSE_HOURS_HIGH`, `RESPONSE_HOURS_NORMAL` and `RESPONSE_HOURS_LOW` (defaults 4, 24, 72, 168).
2. Deploy 1.5.0 with `DUE_TIMES` unset. At startup it fills missing due times from each ticket's own creation time and
   priority and atomically saves the whole file before listening. All statuses are backfilled. It does not change
   ticket update times, audit history or notifications. A save failure aborts startup. New tickets also persist due times.
3. Inspect the file's tickets: every record now has `due`. Keep a copy of this prepared file. Restart with
   `DUE_TIMES=on` to expose due on ticket responses and enable `GET /tickets?overdue=true`.

The feature flag controls API output and query handling; with it off, `overdue` is ignored as in 1.4.0. Without a data
file the same preparation happens in memory. A later priority or response-hours change never recalculates a stored due.
Backfill is idempotent and happens before serving even if the flag is enabled on the first start.

To disable the feature, unset `DUE_TIMES` and restart. To roll back the binary, stop 1.5.0 and start 1.4.0 on the same
file. The document remains version 1 with additive ticket fields, so 1.4.0 loads every ticket, audit entry and outbox
notification. Its writer drops unknown fields including due; if it writes the file, retain the prepared backup for
recovering original deadlines before enabling due times again. Do not replace live tickets with an older backup.
''';p.write_text(s)
p=Path('docs/api.md');s=p.read_text();s+='''
## Due times (opt-in)

When `DUE_TIMES=on`, every ticket returned by create, get, list, patch or transition includes `due`, an ISO UTC timestamp.
It is creation time plus the configured response hours for its initial priority and never moves when priority changes.
Clients cannot supply or patch `due`.

`GET /tickets?overdue=true` selects open and in-progress tickets with due strictly before the current time. Resolved and
closed tickets are excluded. The overdue restriction applies in addition to existing status/priority filters and before
cursor pagination. `overdue=false` adds no restriction; other values answer 400 invalid. With the flag off, ticket
responses omit due and the service ignores the overdue query parameter as it did before.
''';p.write_text(s)
p=Path('CHANGELOG.md');s=p.read_text().replace('## 1.4.0', '## 1.5.0 (2026-11-15)\n\n- Persist fixed due times, backfill existing tickets before serving, and configure response hours through environment variables.\n- Opt in with `DUE_TIMES=on` to show due times and filter active overdue tickets.\n- Keep the version 1 data file readable by 1.4.0 and retain command-line raw column positions.\n\n## 1.4.0');p.write_text(s)
Path('docs/decisions/0009-fixed-due-times.md').write_text('''# 9. Fixed due times with staged exposure

Date: 2026-11-15
Status: Accepted

## Context

The desk promises priority-based response times, needs configurable hours and must be able to roll back to 1.4.0.

## Decision

The store assigns due once, at creation or startup backfill, from creation time and priority. Startup saves missing due
values before the server listens. Persist due as an optional additive field in version 1; keep validating legacy data.
The API exposes due and accepts the overdue filter only with DUE_TIMES=on. Hours are environment settings. Migration
changes neither history nor notifications; it prepares metadata rather than representing an operator ticket edit.

## Consequences

Changing priority or configuration cannot move existing deadlines. Operators can prepare the file with API behavior
unchanged, then enable exposure separately. The 1.4.0 reader ignores due and keeps all tickets; its writer drops unknown
fields, so recovering original deadlines after an old binary writes requires the prepared backup. Raw CLI columns stay
fixed for the weekly report. Existing status/priority filter combination semantics remain unchanged; overdue adds an
active-and-past-due restriction before pagination.
''')
p=Path('docs/decisions/README.md');s=p.read_text();s+='| 9 | [Fixed due times with staged exposure](0009-fixed-due-times.md) | Accepted |\n';p.write_text(s)

Back up DATA_FILE and deploy 1.5.0 with DUE_TIMES unset. At startup the store fills missing due times using each ticket's
creation time and priority, then atomically saves them before listening. Creation also persists a due time while the
feature is off. Inspect the data file to confirm every ticket has `due`, then restart with DUE_TIMES=on. Only this exact
value exposes due in API ticket responses and enables GET /tickets?overdue=true. A failed migration prevents startup.

DUE_HOURS_URGENT/HIGH/NORMAL/LOW take whole hours from 1 through 876000. Changes affect only newly created tickets and
legacy tickets still missing a due time. Priority edits, restarts and feature toggles preserve existing due times.
Backfill changes no audit entries, updated timestamps or notifications.

For rollback stop the service and run release 1.4.0 against the same file. The file remains version 1 with additive
fields, which the old reader ignores, so all tickets remain readable. The old release drops due fields when saving;
before enabling 1.5.0 again, restore preserved due values from the backup, matching by ticket id, if the original promises
must be kept. Tickets created during rollback need backfilling. Do not run concurrent writers.
''';p.write_text(s)
p=Path('docs/api.md');p.write_text(p.read_text()+'''
## Due times

With DUE_TIMES=on every returned ticket includes `due`, an ISO timestamp fixed at creation. The response hours default
to urgent 4, high 24, normal 72 and low 168. Operators configure them through DUE_HOURS_<PRIORITY>. Updating priority does
not change due. Existing tickets receive due times from their own creation time and priority before requests are served.

GET /tickets?overdue=true keeps only open or in_progress tickets with due strictly before the current time, combining
with the existing filters and cursor pagination. overdue=false leaves the listing unfiltered; other overdue values return
400 while enabled. With DUE_TIMES off, responses omit due and ignore the overdue parameter, as in earlier releases.
''')

Response promises must survive priority and configuration changes. Each ticket stores an additive ISO `due` field,
